newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds down with U.S., bad mood lingers.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds down with U.S., bad mood lingers.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished lower Thursday, dragged down by U.S. Treasuries and concerns that the sour mood that has hung over the market for days may linger on.
The market did, however, muster to contain its losses amid thin trade. "There are strong support levels," said a trader at a large foreign bank.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was at 117.25, down $0.35, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 slipped 3/4 to 79-3/4.
"The most prudent thing to do is to stay at the sidelines of the market but if the 'bad mood' is accentuated opportunities may present themselves," said Banco Frances in an investor note.
Banco Frances suggested that if there are further declines, Argentina's FRB, the Bocon Previsional 2 and peso-denominated Bocon Previsional 1 should be considered.

But traders did not think the sluggish market mode of late would end this week. Possibly there could be a bounce next week, but with the U.S. presidential election approaching there could be new uncertainty.

This week's worries have concentrated on a softer Mexican peso, which is feared could impact local markets, and corruption accusations by former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo of government officials.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 7.05 percent from 7.25 percent.
